supporting_observations.claim: The periodic HTTPS activity is attributable to gradebookproupd.exe running as raul.diaz from the user's AppData\Local\GradeBookPro directory, rather than the inventory-listed Program Files location.

The updater made repeated proxy CONNECT requests to update.gradebookpro.co at approximately five-minute intervals during the alert window; this differs from the inventory-listed update.gradebookpro.com domain.

Most recorded requests to the .co hostname received proxy status 200, while the 13:52 request received status 502. The records identify the requested hostname and proxy outcome, but do not establish what content was exchanged with the remote server.
The process, location, and hostname discrepancies make the activity suspicious, but the available records do not establish that the executable or destination is malicious.

known_telemetry_limitations: The proxy records show CONNECT tunnels for the updater requests, not inspected HTTPS request or response content.
The supplied records do not include the updater's hash, signature status, download provenance, or a verified comparison with an authorized GradeBook Pro binary.
The records do not establish ownership or reputation of update.gradebookpro.co, or whether it is an authorized alias for the inventory-listed domain.
claims_not_established: Whether gradebookproupd.exe in the user's AppData directory is an authentic, authorized updater or a masquerading executable.
Whether update.gradebookpro.co is controlled by the approved GradeBook Pro provider.
Whether the successful proxy tunnels carried a benign update check, a software update, or other content.
additional_evidence_needed: Collect the updater file's hash, digital-signature details, creation and download provenance, and compare it with a known-good authorized version.
Verify the .co hostname's ownership and relationship to the approved .com domain using authoritative vendor information and domain/DNS evidence.
Obtain endpoint or proxy TLS inspection and response details, if available, to determine what the repeated connections exchanged.
unrelated_findings: Separate ticket: WS-RDIAZ-01 connected through the proxy to dl.dropboxusercontent.com; this is a cloud/file-sharing service not listed as approved. These records do not attribute the connection to the GradeBook updater. (T285-00171, T285-00172)

Separate ticket: the proxy host attempted connections to WS-RDIAZ-01 on SSH, SMB, proxy, 8443, and RDP ports; the records show rejected or reset attempts. This is separate from the workstation's outbound updater traffic. (T285-00038, T285-00039, T285-00040, T285-00041, T285-00070, T285-00073, T285-00074)

Separate ticket: a SYSTEM PowerShell process launched a scheduled service-health.ps1 script with ExecutionPolicy Bypass and recorded explicit use of svc-grades credentials for FILE-ORC-01. The supplied evidence does not connect this activity to the alerted HTTPS requests. (T285-00191, T285-00192, T285-00199)

Separate ticket: DC-ORC-01 recorded a successful FILE-ORC-01 network logon for tess.hart from the WS-RDIAZ-01 address. This is not part of the alerted outbound HTTPS activity. (T285-00178, T285-00179, T285-00180)
